concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bounds: f = O(g) means f is at most a constant times g for all sufficiently large inputs.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Finite sums of powers of a formal variable with coefficients, with their addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with real a and b and i squared equal to -1, with modulus and complex conjugation.

concepts.name: Basic Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine reads and writes symbols on tape cells under a finite control, and a multitape machine gives each tape its own head.

concepts.name: Fixed-tape Turing machine model
concepts.gloss: A machine with one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, in which each step moves each head by at most one cell and running time counts these steps.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: The 1971 proposal that n log n is the optimal order of growth for multiplying integers on a multitape Turing machine; the main result refutes it in the fixed-tape model.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Established fixed-tape integer multiplier
concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's deterministic fixed-tape multiplication of N-bit integers in O(N log N) time, which the new algorithm calls as an ordinary subroutine on shorter records.

evidence.quote: We use the established $O(N\log N)$ integer multiplier of

concepts.name: Elementary stream operations
concepts.gloss: Linear-time scans on a fixed number of tapes that permute or move digits at chosen positions, apply fixed pointwise maps to aligned streams, and split whole rows cyclically into W streams of equal volume.

evidence.quote: takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

concepts.name: Logical volume
concepts.gloss: The number V of stored data bits in an array, not counting work tapes or duplicate streams; every tape cost is measured against V.

evidence.quote: is the number of stored data bits

concepts.name: Address fields and rows
concepts.gloss: An array is indexed by a complete lexicographic product of address fields and stored in that order, and a row is the complete block of entries at one fixed prefix and row index.

evidence.quote: When one address field is designated as a row field

concepts.name: Row splitting into role streams
concepts.gloss: Distributing the rows of an array cyclically among W role streams, so that each stream has the same shape and volume V/W and gates act pointwise on matching addresses.

evidence.quote: Distribute rows cyclically among the $W$ roles

concepts.name: Controlled cyclic shifts
concepts.gloss: A cyclic shift of a target field by an offset computed from the preceding control fields, together with multiplication by fixed rational units, all done in linear time on tapes.

evidence.quote: their target field follows their control fields

concepts.name: Linear algebra over a field
concepts.gloss: Vector spaces, linear maps and matrices, with subspaces, bilinear forms, orthogonal complements and tensor products, as used by the finite networks and their labels.

evidence.quote: choose an invertible linear operator

concepts.name: Restoration of arbitrary scratch values
concepts.gloss: A linear computation whose auxiliary wires may start with arbitrary values and end with the same values, so that an exchange of two banks can be performed without knowing the scratch contents (the transparent-computation idea of Buhrman et al.).

evidence.quote: This cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear

concepts.name: Triple-subset exchange network
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network whose banks are indexed by triples of three-element subsets of a 100-element set, which exchanges two banks with a sign while restoring all scratch wires, using eight rows of copy, gather, scatter and side-injection operations.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets

concepts.name: Frames on network vertices
concepts.gloss: An invertible linear operator attached to each gate, source and sink of a network, which changes the stored representation of a wire's array so that every gate acts pointwise and the endpoint operators are the only net effect.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame

concepts.name: Subspace labels and orthogonal residuals
concepts.gloss: A nondegenerate subspace attached to each network vertex, with one label containing the other along every edge, so that the dimension of the orthogonal residual on an edge measures the cost of its frame change.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.

concepts.name: Rank saving s < Wm
concepts.gloss: The inequality that the number s of smaller calls is less than W times m, where W is the number of wires and m the label dimension, which is the source of the power saving.

evidence.quote: number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$

concepts.title: Rank saving $s < Wm$

symbols.name: smaller-call count
symbols.meaning: The number of smaller calls made by one network invocation, the sum of the rational ranks of all edge matrix differences.

symbols.name: wire count
symbols.meaning: The number of wires in the network, including its scratch wires.

symbols.name: label dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the ambient label space, which is h cubed for the set size h = 100.

concepts.name: Volume-normalized recursion
concepts.gloss: A recursion in which cost per unit volume is multiplied by s/W at each level, with s/W below m to the power tau, so that the total cost is O(e^tau) per unit volume for chunks of e = m^k digits.

evidence.quote: is the source of the power saving

concepts.name: Lower-triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Every rational matrix of rank a factors as an invertible lower-triangular matrix times a partial permutation matrix with exactly a ones, times another invertible lower-triangular matrix.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Matrix shear of address fields
concepts.gloss: The map (H, D) to (H + AD, D) on two groups of address fields for a fixed rational matrix A of rank a, performed with exactly a interchanges of field pairs and linear extra work.

evidence.quote: can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit

concepts.name: Finite circuit as address permutation
concepts.gloss: The transfer of a finite bit circuit with rational vertex matrices whose rank sum is below Wm into a permutation of address fields that applies the same shear to every wire role.

evidence.quote: Assign a rational $m\times m$ matrix to each terminal and to each gate

concepts.name: Power-width chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: The interchange of two disjoint equal chunks of e = m^k digits in O(V e^tau) time, by splitting rows into W role streams, applying one shear per unit of rank on the streams, and recursing with the same fixed tapes.

evidence.quote: The chunks can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time

concepts.name: Arbitrary-width chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: The interchange of two equal bit chunks of arbitrary width u in O(V u^tau) time, by padding to a power of the radix, moving high digits into a row field, and handling the remaining width as a sum of power-width pieces in base m.

evidence.quote: Write the remaining width in base $m$

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadic
concepts.gloss: A complex number whose real and imaginary parts are dyadic rationals, that is, have power-of-two denominators.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics

concepts.name: Guard bits
concepts.gloss: Extra fractional and integer bits reserved in each coefficient so that every intermediate value of an exact butterfly layer is represented exactly, with a width bound that grows only as a fixed power of the number of selected axes.

evidence.quote: Thus reserving \(p+\Delta\)

concepts.name: Normalized two-point butterfly
concepts.gloss: The map (u, v) to ((u + v)/2, (u − v)/2) applied to a pair of coefficients, the basic step of the synthetic transforms.

evidence.quote: two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: Two-point phase kernel
concepts.gloss: The 2 by 2 matrix C = aI + bX with a = (1 + i)/2 and b = (1 − i)/2, the Hadamard conjugate of the phase diag(1, i), which satisfies C² = X and C⁴ = I and is the one-bit kernel from which phase frames are built.

evidence.quote: C=H\mathsf SH=aI+bX

concepts.name: Binary phase frames
concepts.gloss: Frames indexed by binary subspace labels, built from the Hadamard transform and phases i raised to the Hamming weight of each label's projection, so that each edge change is a product of two-point phase kernels, one per residual basis vector.

evidence.quote: Use the complex scalar network and binary labels.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit XOR
concepts.gloss: A linear-time operation that XORs the selected bits of one address chunk slot into the corresponding selected bits of another for all selected positions at once, using eight packed rotations of guarded segments followed by deterministic repair of the few addresses whose guards fail.

evidence.quote: We implement a binary row addition on corresponding selected bits in two

concepts.name: Disk-grid arrays
concepts.gloss: Arrays of coefficients lying in the complex unit disk and on the grid 2^(−p) times the Gaussian integers, which hold every approximate value in the algorithm.

evidence.quote: A disk array has norm at most one.

concepts.name: Truncation to the precision grid
concepts.gloss: Rounding each real and imaginary part of a coefficient toward zero onto the grid of spacing 2^(−p), which keeps arrays in the disk and moves each entry by less than sqrt(2) times 2^(−p).

evidence.quote: A single truncation follows the completed contractive layer.

concepts.name: Approximate roots of unity
concepts.gloss: Disk-grid approximations of the roots of unity e^(2πi j/k) with error below 2^(−p), computable in time O(max(p, log k)^(1+δ)) and used for the phase twists.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: The application of the normalized two-point butterfly to the same selected bit position in each of D address chunks at once, computed exactly through binary phase frames and truncated once, at cost O(V d^(λ')) with λ' below one instead of D separate passes.

evidence.quote: one selects the same bit position in each of at most $d$

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.gloss: The ring of polynomials with complex coefficients of degree less than r, where r is a power of two and y^r is identified with −1, so that multiplication by a power of y is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: polynomial variable
symbols.meaning: The formal variable of the ring, whose powers serve as roots of unity in the transforms.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a record, which is a power of two.

concepts.name: Polynomial roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The observation that powers of y in the polynomial ring are roots of unity whose multiplication is a signed shift, so a transform over the ring can use them as twiddle factors.

evidence.quote: serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The convolution of two arrays indexed by a product of cyclic groups, in which each output entry sums products of input entries whose indices are added modulo the axis lengths.

evidence.quote: let $*$ denote cyclic convolution in the displayed

concepts.name: Normalized discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The map (F_q u)_k = (1/q) times the sum over j of u_j e^(−2πi jk/q) on vectors of length q, together with its opposite-sign partner F_q^+, which turns cyclic convolution into pointwise products up to a known factor.

evidence.quote: Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction

concepts.name: Contraction
concepts.gloss: A linear map that does not increase the maximum-modulus norm, so that an error in its input is not amplified when it is applied to an approximation.

evidence.quote: Both $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B_0$ are contractions.

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A normalized radix-two transform over the polynomial ring whose twiddle factors are powers of y, so each round is a parallel butterfly followed by a signed shift and the whole transform is a contraction.

evidence.quote: synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle

concepts.name: Positional layout of transform axes
concepts.gloss: A positional permutation of record addresses that places the selected bits of all participating axes at a common offset in consecutive K-bit chunks, realized by single-bit moves and chunk interchanges so that the simultaneous layer applies.

concepts.name: Synthetic transform on fixed tapes

concepts.name: Retained frequency order
concepts.gloss: The stored record order produced by the forward synthetic transforms, which is preserved through a pointwise product so that the opposite transform consumes it without extra data movement.

evidence.quote: retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product

concepts.name: Phase twist of the last coordinate
concepts.gloss: The isomorphism from the cyclic group algebra of length r to the polynomial ring that sends x to ζy with ζ = e^(πi/r), implemented by multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k and undone by multiplying by ζ^(−k).

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing
concepts.gloss: Evaluating two integer polynomials at a large base 2^(4p) so that one exact integer product yields all coefficient products, with signed carries recovered by centered residues; it is a signed form of Kronecker substitution.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Computed chirp transform
